messages.subject: Argument "E" in the INLA package
parts:
Hello INLA Experts,

I am using INLA package in which my dependent variable is observed cases of a disease like this
formula <- Y ~
  f(id, model = "besag", graph = g, scale.model = TRUE) +
  f(id1, model = "iid")

where Y is the observed cases

res <- inla(formula,
  family = "poisson", data = map@data,
  E = Expected, control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE)
)
 In the above Expected is the expected number of cases.
 Now I am aware if I use E in the model I'll get estimates of risk as my fitted values.
But my requirement is to produce estimate of Observed cases instead of risk
Like (Y^hat) . In rejigging the above code I removed E from the arguments
and ran it like below.


res <- inla(formula,
  family = "poisson", data = map@data,
   control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE)

Will this produce what I require(estimate of Observed cases rather than estimates of risk).

Thanks!!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Argument "E" in the INLA package
parts:
I think this is what you want (I just extended the demo(Bym) )

Best
H



data(Germany)
g = system.file("demodata/germany.graph", package="INLA")
source(system.file("demodata/Bym-map.R", package="INLA"))
Germany = cbind(Germany,region.struct=Germany$region)

formula1 = Y ~ f(region.struct,model="besag",graph=g, scale.model =
TRUE) +
f(region,model="iid")
result1 = inla(formula1,family="poisson",data=Germany, E=E,
control.compute = list(config = TRUE))

xx <- inla.posterior.sample(10000, result1)
yy <- inla.posterior.sample.eval(
function(E) return(rpois(length(Predictor), E*exp(Predictor))),
xx, E = Germany$E)
yy.hat <- rowMeans(yy)
Bym.map(yy.hat)
